title: Second sense: natural as what every appetite seeks
source_text: XV. Item naturale dicitur id in quod naturaliter fertur cujusque appetitus. Et etiam sic concedit immortalitatem homini naturalem esse, & mortem contra naturam, quoniam omnes natura appetunt immortalitatem, mortem vero refugiunt.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise that is called natural toward which the appetite of each thing is naturally borne. And in this way too he concedes that immortality is natural to man, and death against nature, since all by nature desire immortality, but flee death.
pass_b_english: Again, what each thing's appetite naturally tends toward is called natural. In this sense too he grants that immortality is natural to man and death against nature, because everyone by nature longs for immortality and shrinks from death.

choices.why: Estius concedes the point within one sense only; 'grants' keeps that limited concession.
